reply.title: The Highest Point of a Vertical Throw
reply.story: When you toss a ball straight up into the air, it slows down as it rises, pauses for a brief instant at its highest point, and then speeds up as it falls back down. Watching this happen, it is natural to wonder about that exact moment at the very top. Since the ball's upward motion stops completely and its velocity is zero for a fraction of a second, does its acceleration also drop to zero? Common sense might suggest that if something is stopped, nothing is happening to it. But let us look closer at how velocity changes from one moment to the next. Even at the very top, the ball's speed is continuously changing from upward to downward. That ongoing change is acceleration, driven by the constant pull of gravity.
reply.cardDescription: Explore what happens to a ball's velocity and acceleration when thrown straight up. Discover why velocity is zero at the apex while acceleration remains constant.
reply.instructions: Adjust the launch speed and press Play to observe the ball's motion. Use the scrubber to pause at the top and examine the readouts.

words.motion_top: At the apex, velocity is zero
